newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday June 25.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Italy's cross-party constitutional reform commission approved proposals for parliamentary changes and rejected an amendment put forward by the centre-left on a two-round electoral system (all).

* The European Commission said Italy's economic goals and reforms identified in a recent economic programme for 1998-2000 were good and appropriate. EU commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy warned Italy's "moment of truth" regarding qualification for the EU's single currency would come in September when it is expected to adopt budgetary measures for 1998 (all).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he expected interest rates to fall as financial markets became convinced of the structural nature of lower inflation and healthier public accounts (all).

* A report by Italian industrialists' group Confindustria said Italy's deficit will come in at 3.4 percent of GDP in 1997 if interest rates remain unchanged and the government does not introduce fresh budget measures. Confindustria expected the deficit/GDP ratio to fall to 3.0 percent in 1998 against a government target of 2.8 percent, while GDP will not grow by more than one percent in 1997 (Sole 24 Ore).
* Treasury Ministry sources say sale of state controlled telephone directory publisher Seat should take place by end of July (Il Sole).

* Treasury Ministry sources also say "greenshoe" of third tranche of energy group ENI could be exercised as public share offer currently underway is going so well and by second day of offer was already oversubscribed (Il Sole, La Repubblica).

* Merchant bank Mediobanca has launched a 150 billion lire bond linked to the performance of five European telecoms companies, British Telecom, Deutsche Telekom, Portugal Telecom, Stet and Telefonica de Espana (Il Sole).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
